10.1.intro: A sign-up form asks visitors for their email or phone. It feeds every email you send. A good one signs up 3 to 10 of every 100 visitors.

steps.say: Pick one reason to sign up: dollars off (like $10 off) if your orders are big, percent off (like 10% off) if they're small, a free gift, early access, or a competition entry.
steps.check: Your form has one clear reason to sign up.
steps.lost: Pick 10% off. You can change it later.

steps.say: In your email app (Klaviyo, Omnisend or Shopify Email), build a form with steps: first an easy one-click question ("What are you shopping for?"), then email, then phone.
steps.check: The form asks an easy question first. Small yeses lead to bigger ones.
steps.lost: Make the first step one easy question.

steps.say: Show the form after about 5 to 8 seconds or 30% scroll. On computers, also show it when the mouse moves to leave. Hide it from people already signed up.
steps.check: It shows at the right time, and never to people already on your list.
steps.careful: Game forms (spin to win) can get more sign-ups. Watch the cost of the discounts and the quality of the list.
steps.lost: Set it to show after 5 seconds.

steps.say: Sell to several regions? Add location rules so each region sees offers and text sign-ups that suit it.
steps.check: Overseas visitors see an offer that makes sense for them.
steps.lost: One country only? Skip this card.

steps.say:
After 2 weeks, check and improve.

1. Open the form's report. Find the sign-up rate.
2. Change one thing (the offer, headline or timing). Wait another 2 weeks.
steps.check: You're above 3 sign-ups per 100 visitors, or a test is running to get there. With a strong offer, 6 to 10 is possible.
steps.lost: Look at the sign-up rate. Change one thing.

steps.say:
Put a form inside a page too, not just as a pop-up.

1. In your email app (like Klaviyo), make a new **Embedded** form.
2. Copy its form ID or code.
3. In Shopify, click **Online Store**, then **Themes**, then **Customize**.
4. Open the page you want (home or "About").
5. Click **Add section** or **Add block**.
6. Pick your email app's form block (or **Custom Liquid**).
7. Paste the form ID or code.
8. Click **Save**.
steps.check: The form shows inside the page, and a test sign-up lands in your list within a minute.
steps.lost: Make an **Embedded** form. Add it to your home page.

10.2.intro: A flow is a set of emails or texts that sends itself when someone does something. Five main flows earn money every day, even while you sleep.

steps.say: Set up the **Welcome** flow. It starts when someone joins your list.
steps.check: New subscribers get your first email within minutes.
steps.lost: Turn on Welcome. That's the first one.

steps.say: Set up **Browse abandonment**. It starts when someone looks at a product but doesn't add it to cart.
steps.check: Browsers get a reminder of what they looked at.
steps.lost: Turn on Browse abandonment.

steps.say: Set up **Cart abandonment**. It starts when someone adds to cart but doesn't start checkout.
steps.check: They get a reminder within a few hours.
steps.lost: Turn on Cart abandonment.

steps.say: Set up **Checkout abandonment**. It starts when someone begins checkout but doesn't pay.
steps.check: These keen shoppers get a reminder within about an hour.
steps.lost: Turn on Checkout abandonment.

steps.say: Set up **Post-purchase**. It starts when someone buys.
steps.check: New buyers get a thank-you, how-to tips and an idea for something else.
steps.lost: Turn on Post-purchase.

steps.say: Then add extras, one at a time: win-back, back in stock, price drop, time to reorder, VIP, birthday, sunset (removing people who never open), review request, and a cross-sell after the first buy.
steps.check: Your list of flows grows month by month.
steps.lost: Add one extra flow this month.

10.3.intro: Emails that get clicks feel personal and have one clear job.

steps.say: Take turns: a plain email from the founder (pictures are fine), then a designed email.
steps.check: Your next four emails include at least one founder-style email.
steps.lost: Write one short, plain email from you.

steps.say: Use what people told you in forms (like product interest, skin type or size) to pick what to show them.
steps.check: Different people see different product picks.
steps.lost: Use one answer, like size, to pick products.

steps.say: Give each email one main button.
steps.check: Every email has one obvious next step.
steps.careful: Only use countdown timers for real deadlines. When time's up, show a message, not zeros.
steps.lost: Keep one button. Remove the rest.

10.4.intro: A segment is a group on your list who share something. Sending to the right group keeps you out of spam.

steps.say: In your email app, make segments: active in the last 30, 60 and 90 days, buyers, repeat buyers, and VIPs (your best customers).
steps.check: The segments show live counts.
steps.lost: Make one segment: active in the last 90 days.

steps.say: Add window shoppers (looked lately, never bought), lapsed buyers (used to buy, stopped) and product-interest segments.
steps.check: You can reach people at every stage.
steps.lost: Make a window shoppers segment.

steps.say: Send most campaign emails to the people active in the last 60 or 90 days.
steps.check: More people open, and fewer mark you as spam.
steps.lost: Send your next email to the 90-day active group.

10.5.intro: A campaign is a one-off email, like a newsletter. Start slow and build up.

steps.say: Start with 2 emails a month. After a month, go weekly. Then 2 to 4 a week if people still open and click.
steps.check: You have a written send schedule.
steps.lost: Plan 2 emails this month.

steps.say: Fill your schedule from this list: new arrivals, how-to tips, customer stories, behind the scenes, founder notes, gift guides, myth busting, customer photos, seasonal moments, limited bundles, rare flash sales.
steps.check: You have a month of email ideas.
steps.lost: Pick two ideas from the list.

10.6.intro: A monthly check shows where emails leak money. Fix the weakest step first.

steps.say: Open your email app's reports. Write down last month's flow and campaign numbers from the lesson's table.
steps.check: You have one line of numbers for flows and one for campaigns.
steps.lost: Write down opens and clicks for last month.

steps.say: Find the weakest step. Low opens? Fix the subject line. Low clicks? Fix the content and button. Clicks but few orders? Fix the landing page.
steps.check: You have one fix to make this month.
steps.lost: Which is lowest: opens, clicks or orders? Fix that one.

10.7.intro: A fair split test shows what your list likes. One change, two big groups, one written guess.

steps.say: Write your guess. Example: "A question in the subject line gets more opens."
steps.check: The test has a written guess.
steps.lost: Write one sentence: what you think will win.

steps.say: Change only one thing (subject, send time, offer or layout). Split the list into two groups of at least a few thousand each, if you can.
steps.check: The test is fair and big enough to read.
steps.lost: Change just the subject line.

steps.say: Write down the result. Use the winner from now on.
steps.check: Your test log grows and emails get better each month.
steps.lost: Write who won. Use it next time.

10.8.intro: Deliverability means your emails land in the inbox, not spam. Most of it is set up once.

steps.say: In your email app's domain settings, follow the guide to add SPF, DKIM and DMARC records at your domain host. They prove your emails really come from you.
steps.check: The email app shows your sending domain as verified or authenticated.
steps.lost: Open your email app's domain settings. Follow its guide.

steps.say: New account? Warm up slowly. Each send goes to no more than about 1.5 times as many people as the last, most active people first. Example: 1,000, then 1,500, then 2,250.
steps.check: Sends grow steadily with no bounce or spam spikes.
steps.lost: Send to your most active people first.

steps.say: Remove bad addresses, like typos (gmial.com). Set up a sunset flow for people who never open.
steps.check: Your list only has people you can reach who care.
steps.lost: Search for "gmial" and remove those.

steps.say: Each week, check bounce rates by email provider. Avoid ALL CAPS, lots of exclamation marks, and emails that are just one picture.
steps.check: You spot trouble with one provider (like only Outlook bouncing) early.
steps.lost: Check bounces once this week.

10.9.intro: Email apps often charge by how many people are on your list. Cleaning it saves money and helps you reach inboxes.

steps.say: Suppress or remove people who haven't opened or clicked in 180 days.
steps.check: The number of people you pay for drops.
steps.lost: Find people quiet for 180 days. Suppress them.

steps.say: Archive old lists you don't send to anymore.
steps.check: Only active lists are left.
steps.lost: Archive one old list.

steps.say: If each person on your list costs more than they're worth to you, compare two other email apps.
steps.check: You know if you should stay or switch.
steps.lost: Look at one other app's prices.

10.10.intro: Texts get read fast but cost more than email. Save them for big moments.

steps.say: Add a text step to the welcome flow and the checkout reminder, for people who didn't act on the email.
steps.check: Texts only go out where email didn't work.
steps.lost: Add one text to the checkout reminder.

steps.say: Use texts for sale launches and last chance messages.
steps.check: Your sale plan has two texts.
steps.lost: Plan one text for your next sale launch.

steps.say: Register your sender name where the law needs it (like in some countries). Respect quiet hours. Keep each text short with one link.
steps.check: Texts come from your registered name, at sensible times, with one link.
steps.lost: Keep texts short, with one link.

10.11.intro: WhatsApp works well where your customers already use it, especially for VIPs and pricey products.

steps.say: Set up WhatsApp Business. Only message people who said yes.
steps.check: You have a WhatsApp list of people who opted in.
steps.lost: Download WhatsApp Business.

steps.say: Get your marketing message templates approved. Set up quick replies for common questions.
steps.check: You can send approved offers and answer common questions in one tap.
steps.lost: Make one quick reply.

steps.say: Use chat for VIPs, launches and selling through conversation.
steps.check: Big customers can buy just by chatting.
steps.lost: Message one VIP about a launch.

10.12.intro: A loyalty program rewards people who buy again. It only pays when enough people already come back.

steps.say: Check your repeat purchase rate in Shopify **Analytics > Reports > Customers over time**. Only start loyalty if more than about 15 to 20% of customers already buy again.
steps.check: You know if loyalty is worth it yet.
steps.lost: Find your repeat rate. Is it over 15%?

steps.say: Pick rewards your margin can afford (points or cashback). Add VIP levels with early access.
steps.check: The program is set up and the rewards are costed.
steps.lost: Choose one reward you can afford.

steps.say: Add referral rewards for customers who bring a friend.
steps.check: Customers can share a referral link.
steps.lost: Turn on referrals.

steps.say: After 90 days, check how the repeat purchase rate changed.
steps.check: You know if the program changed what people do.
steps.lost: Put a 90-day reminder in your calendar.

10.13.intro: Big sales depend on email and texts. A fixed plan from tease to thank-you means every part gets a message, without spamming.

steps.say:
Before the sale, build an early-access list.

1. Two weeks before, turn on an "early access" sign-up form.
2. Each week, send one teaser email to that list.
steps.check: Your early-access list is growing.
steps.lost: Turn on an early-access form 2 weeks before.

steps.say: On launch day, send one email and one text.
steps.check: Your list hears about the sale first.
steps.lost: Send one email on launch day.

steps.say: In the middle of the sale, send a new reason to buy (a new product, a bundle or a gift).
steps.check: The middle of the sale has fresh news.
steps.lost: Send one email with a new bundle.

steps.say: On the last day, send a last chance email and text.
steps.check: Everyone hears it's ending.
steps.lost: Send one "last chance" email.

steps.say: After the sale, send new buyers thanks, how-to tips, results and a small time-limited deal. Switch your abandonment flows back from the sale versions.
steps.check: New buyers are looked after and flows are back to normal.
steps.lost: Switch your flows back to normal.

10.15.intro: Ask one question, save the answer and send each person products that fit them.

steps.say: Pick one question that splits your customers into groups. For example: "What is your skin type?", "Who are you shopping for?" or "Which size is your dog?"
steps.check: One question with 3 to 5 simple answers.
steps.lost: Pick one easy question with a few answers.

steps.say: Add the question to your sign-up form, as a second step after the email box (Lesson 10.1).
steps.check: New subscribers can tap one answer in a second.
steps.lost: Put it after the email box.

steps.say: In your email app, check the answer saves to each person's profile. Most apps call this a custom field or profile property.
steps.check: You can see the answer on a test profile.
steps.lost: Check the answer saves.

steps.say: In your welcome flow (Lesson 10.2), add a split based on the answer. Send each group an email with the 3 products that suit them best.
steps.check: Each group gets product picks that fit them.
steps.lost: Send each group the products that suit them.

steps.say: For people who did not answer, add a one-click question in the second welcome email. Make each answer a button that saves the answer.
steps.check: More of your list has an answer.
steps.lost: Ask again with buttons in email 2.

steps.say: After 30 days, compare clicks and sales from the matched emails with your old welcome emails (Lesson 10.6).
steps.check: You know if the answers lift sales. Then use the same groups in sale emails (Lesson 10.4).
steps.lost: Compare after 30 days.

10.16.intro: Emailing people who ignored you for months can land you in spam. Wake them up slowly before a big sale.

steps.say: In your email app, make groups by last open or click: 30, 60, 90 and 180 days. Add people who joined in the last 15 days to the 30-day group.
steps.check: Four groups with numbers in them.
steps.lost: Make one group: opened or clicked in 90 days.

steps.say: Make a sleeping group: got 5+ emails, no opens or clicks in 180 days.
steps.check: You know how many are asleep.
steps.lost: Find people who never open.

steps.say: In normal weeks, email the 90-day group only.
steps.check: Normal emails go to readers.
steps.lost: Send to the 90-day group.

steps.say: 2 to 3 weeks before the sale, send 1 or 2 short wake-up emails to the 91 to 180 day people, with one reason to click.
steps.check: Some come back into your 90-day group.
steps.lost: Send one 'early access' email to quieter people.

steps.say: Make each send no more than about 1.5 times bigger than the last: 4,000, then 6,000, then 9,000.
steps.check: Sends grow step by step.
steps.lost: Grow each send by half, not more.

steps.say: Only on the biggest sale days, send to the whole 180-day group. Check unsubscribes and spam complaints after each send.
steps.check: You go back to the smaller group if either jumps.
steps.lost: Watch unsubscribes after each send.

steps.say: Turn on a goodbye flow for sleeping people: two short emails asking if they still want to hear from you. Stop emailing anyone who doesn't click.
steps.check: Your list stays healthy.
steps.careful: Clicks are a more honest sign than opens.
steps.lost: Send one 'still want our emails?' email.

10.17.intro: Some customers buy again and again. Some buy once. Plan your ads, sales and emails around which kind you have.

steps.say: In Shopify, open **Analytics > Reports** and find the customer cohort report. Write the share who bought again in 12 months, and the usual days to the second order.
steps.check: Two numbers, like 22% and 45 days.
steps.lost: Find how many customers bought twice.

steps.say: Under about 20% is low repeat. Over about 30% is high repeat. In between is middle.
steps.check: Your store has a label.
steps.lost: Pick low, middle or high.

steps.say: Low repeat: pay no more for a new customer than their first-order profit. High repeat: you can add proven repeat profit from the next 12 months.
steps.check: One 'most I'll pay' number.
steps.lost: Use first-order profit as your limit.

steps.say: Low repeat: fewer, bigger sales for new buyers. High repeat: early access for past buyers and small list-only events.
steps.check: Your calendar fits your store.
steps.lost: Plan one sale that fits your type.

steps.say: Send a reorder email a little before the usual second order. 45 days usual? Send on day 38.
steps.check: A reorder email is live.
steps.lost: Add one reminder email.

steps.say: Pick three products often bought together. Add them in **Apps > Search & Discovery > Product recommendations**, and in one follow-up email.
steps.check: Three pairs show on product pages and in an email.
steps.lost: Pick one pair that goes together.
